body_text:
Fix a formal deductive system equipped with a collection of
logical axioms and rules of inference. A *derivation* (or
formal deduction) of a sentence $\varphi$ from a set of
premises $\Gamma$ is a finite tree or sequence of sentences
$\varphi_1, \varphi_2, \dots, \varphi_n = \varphi$ such that
each $\varphi_i$ is either an axiom, an element of $\Gamma$, or
the direct result of applying an allowable inference rule to
earlier members of the sequence.

When such a derivation exists, we write
$\Gamma \vdash \varphi$. Whereas the relation
$\Gamma \models \varphi$ is semantic and concerns infinite
classes of interpretations, the relation
$\Gamma \vdash \varphi$ is purely syntactic and finite: a
computer algorithm can inspect and verify every step of a
formal derivation in finite time.
